item.title: ROSTAFA & COMPANY: 2PAC REVISITED — Sat Sep 12, 3:00 PM — Montclair Brewery
item.description: Kendee Love I’M TAKING THE STAGE FOR PAC! On Saturday, September 12th, I’ll be performing at Montclair Brewery for 2PAC REVISITED, a special celebration of the life, artistry, and legacy of Tupac Amaru Shakur. 2Pac Revisited brings together poets, rappers, singers, dancers, and musicians to honor Tupac, not simply for his fame, but for his humanity, artistry, and love for his people. Even more importantly, this event is about giving back. Proceeds will help raise awareness and funds for Family Healing Center , a mental health organization located in West Orange, NJ, committed to empowering individuals, strengthening families, and transforming communities through faith, hope, and love. THE DAY IN 3 PARTS: 3 PM | PANEL DISCUSSION Montclair Public Library Auditorium Join award-winning author, minister & professor Dr. Michael Eric Dyson for a conversation about Tupac’s life and artistry. item.title: What Did You Say? Addressing Microaggressions — Fri Sep 18, 4:00 PM — University Hall 1020 - Bard-Blount Family Lecture Hall
item.description:
Omega Phi Chi Multicultural Sorority, Inc. invites students to participate in an educational program focused on understanding and addressing microaggressions. The event will feature an interactive presentation led by the Office of Advocacy and Outreach, providing students with the knowledge and tools to recognize microaggressions, respond effectively, and advocate for themselves and others. Following the presentation, executive members from various registered student organizations—including the Black Student Union (BSU), LadiesFirst, Latin American Student Organization (LASO), Dominican Student Organization (DSO), and other multicultural organizations—will participate in a panel discussion, sharing their lived experiences, perspectives, and advice for fostering a more inclusive campus community.

item.title: Walk at Grover Cleveland Park — Sun Sep 20, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! **MEETING TIME 9:30 AM**
We will meet near the fishing pond entrance of the park, close to Brookside Avenue and the boat house/restrooms. **GPS location: 138 Brookside Ave, Caldwell. Park on the street.**
We will walk for about 60-90 minutes at about a 3 miles/hour pace. The park has a paved path loop that is a little more than a mile. Stay for as many loops as you like.
Grover Cleveland Park in Caldwell/Essex Fells celebrated its centennial in 2013. As the first county park in western Essex County, the site was originally selected for its natural beauty and its potential to provide a space for relaxation and recreation. It contains gentle rolling hills, broad meadows and other environmentally aesthetic features
**Please arrive 5 minutes early, so we can start on time.**

item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Sep 23, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.description:

Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society?
In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today’s global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today’s secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void.
